clue.text: Shy? So drink

indicators.note: the question mark flags a loose device: the conjunction is to be lodged within the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
'so' as a connective, as in 'and so', loosely standing for the conjunction

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bashful person might be persuaded to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SH(AND)Y: the conjunction AND, standing for 'so', sits inside SHY. A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is a light beverage of beer diluted with lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: Make one's home in a small market town

blocks.note: first meaning: to take up residence somewhere
second meaning: a market town in the Yorkshire Dales

explanation.surface: Someone decides to put down roots in a little rural town.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a real market town in North Yorkshire, England, so the second half is a proper noun, not a description.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to establish a permanent residence, and Settle is the name of a Yorkshire market town.

clue.text: Tree in a small enclosure

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for small
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A sapling planted inside a little fenced-off plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar known for its trembling leaves.

clue.text: Playwright has tipple with expert right away

indicators.note: 'away' tells us the letter standing for right is taken out of the word for expert

blocks.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits
an artist is a skilled expert at something
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A writer of plays enjoys a drink with a specialist, then the right-hand person leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAM followed by ARTIST minus its R gives DRAM + ATIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist is a writer of plays, the same as a playwright.

clue.text: Stiffness shown by celebrity at church

blocks.note: a star is a celebrity
CH is the abbreviation for church; 'at' places it next

explanation.surface: A famous person appears rather formal and stiff when attending a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch figuratively means formality or rigidity of manner, from the stiffening agent for fabric.

clue.text: A bulb can be extremely useful in the end

indicators.note: 'extremely' asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of the following word
'in' places the selected letters inside the word for the end

blocks.note: the first and last letters of useful
a tip is the end of something

explanation.surface: A gardener muses that a bulb may prove handy eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads as 'eventually', but 'the end' is a noun phrase for a pointed extremity, with 'in' the placing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip grows from a bulb, so the plant can be called a bulb.

clue.text: Reportedly studied flying machine close to nearest celestial body

indicators.note: 'reportedly' means as heard spoken, so the past tense is taken by its sound
the close of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the past tense read is pronounced like the colour red
an aeroplane
the last letter of nearest

explanation.surface: An astronomer has apparently studied an aircraft near the closest heavenly body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearest celestial body' tempts as the definition, but nearest only supplies its last letter; the red planet is Mars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Planet is the nickname for Mars, a planet and so a celestial body.

clue.text: Watch trapper

blocks.note: first meaning: a pocket watch with a hinged cover protecting the glass
second meaning: one who hunts and catches animals

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an order to keep an eye on a trapper, but 'Watch' is a noun naming a type of timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter is a pocket watch with a protective lid, and also one who pursues game, as a trapper does.

clue.text: Star entertainer needs finest fruit

blocks.note: first meaning: the leading comedian on a bill
second meaning, taken literally: the best piece of a well-known yellow fruit

explanation.surface: A headline performer demands the best fruit in the dressing room.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is slang, from American vaudeville, for the principal comic or most important person.

clue.text: Drink - all do it wildly after a short working day

indicators.note: 'short' means the day's name is cut down to its abbreviation
letters behaving wildly are thrown out of order
'after' puts the jumbled letters behind the other pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
Monday, the first day of the working week
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Everyone goes wild with drink after a brief day at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: MON is the abbreviation of Monday; A + MON + TILLADO.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a medium-dry sherry, a fortified wine from Spain.

clue.text: Hymn from leader of Wesleyans in habit I deem unfit

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so the first letter of the word is kept
something unfit is out of shape, so the letters must be reshaped

blocks.note: the first letter of Wesleyans
the letters to rearrange, with the leader placed among them

explanation.surface: A Methodist leader in vestments judges a hymn unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes in with HABIT I DEEM and the eleven letters are rearranged. Wesleyans are Methodists, followers of John Wesley.
explanation.definitionFit: Abide With Me is a well-known Christian hymn, sung traditionally at the FA Cup Final.

clue.text: Loaded and left Yemeni port

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship, fully loaded, departed from a harbour in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means carrying a heavy load, a synonym of loaded.

clue.text: Girl in hostel in Darlington

indicators.note: 'in' says the name lies inside the following words, running across them

blocks.note: spanning the end of hostel, all of in, and the start of Darlington

explanation.surface: A young woman staying at a hostel in the northern English town of Darlington.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a female first name; 'girl' in crosswords often signals a woman's name.

clue.text: I'm plus one, playing rashly

indicators.note: playing around with letters means trying them in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone bringing a guest to a party, perhaps hastily, or gambling recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on impulse means doing something without forethought, which is acting rashly.

clue.text: This was first brought into town to make parachutes

definitions.note: the answer is a mass noun for the tufts the plural names

indicators.note: 'brought into' means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
one who was first led the field

explanation.surface: A town once made parachutes, a local first.
explanation.walkthrough: THIS + T(LED)OWN. The silky tufts of thistle seeds act as tiny parachutes carrying them on the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Thistledown is the fluffy pappus on thistle seeds, which works like parachutes for dispersal.

clue.text: Musical instruments in largest complex

indicators.note: a complex arrangement is an intricate one, so the letters are tangled together

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An orchestra's instruments housed in the biggest building on site.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are percussion instruments, bent steel bars struck with a beater.

clue.text: Inadvertent mistake concerning landmark

blocks.note: over can mean about, as in fighting over something
a sight is a notable thing to see

explanation.surface: An accidental error relating to a famous monument.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a failure to notice something, an unintentional error.

clue.text: Favoured brief, one man quick on the uptake

blocks.note: to be in with someone is to be favoured
to brief someone is to tell them
I is the Roman numeral one
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A favoured man with a short briefing grasps it at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to inform.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quick on the uptake means understanding fast, a mark of an intelligent person.

clue.text: Girl has drop of Tokay wine

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: Clare is a girl's name
the first letter of Tokay

explanation.surface: A young woman sips a little of a Hungarian dessert wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tokay wine' reads as one phrase, but Tokay gives only a letter and wine is the definition. Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is red wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: A gun each

blocks.note: taken as written
piece is slang for a firearm

explanation.surface: Everyone is issued with one weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece is an adverb meaning for each one, as in a pound apiece.

clue.text: Be eager to land in US city

blocks.note: to long is to yearn eagerly
to beach a boat is to run it ashore

explanation.surface: A traveller can't wait to touch down in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' suggests an aircraft arriving, but here it is a vessel run up onto the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Beach is a large city in southern California.

clue.text: Scholar to study English philosopher

blocks.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
to con is an old word for to study or learn

explanation.surface: An academic sets out to research an English thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an English philosopher and statesman, a founder of empirical science.

clue.text: Take off from Stansted, initially, on holiday

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the initial, the first letter, of the airport's name

blocks.note: the first letter of Stansted
a trip is a holiday or outing

explanation.surface: Flying out of a London airport at the start of a vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests a plane leaving Stansted, a London airport; here it means removing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to take off clothing or a covering.

clue.text: Spanish drink port? Yes, in Germany

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a famous Brazilian port
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether port counts as a Spanish drink and gets a German yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine, fitting the drinks theme, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: RC priest's inside getting a souvenir

indicators.note: 'is inside' places the priest within the abbreviation before it

blocks.note: Roman Catholic, taken as written
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest enters a shrine and takes away a memento.
explanation.walkthrough: R(ELI)C: Eli is the crossword's favourite biblical priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object kept as a reminder of the past, like a keepsake.

clue.text: Kitchener may have had a hand in it

definitions.text: Kitchener may have had a hand in it

blocks.note: surface reading: Lord Kitchener, the British field marshal, involved in some historic affair

blocks.clueFragment: may have had a hand in it
blocks.note: setter's reading: a kitchen worker literally puts a hand inside this padded item

explanation.walkthrough: Kitchener reads as the famous British general; here it is coined for someone who works in a kitchen, whose hand goes inside the item.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded mitt worn to handle hot dishes, which a cook's hand fits into.

clue.text: A herb tea brewed in east

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An infusion of herbs prepared in Eastern fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is an infusion of herbs or flowers, a caffeine-free drink.

clue.text: A guy, relaxed

blocks.note: taken as written
to guy someone is to mock or ridicule them

explanation.surface: A man who is calm and comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a noun for a man, but it is the verb meaning to poke fun at.
explanation.definitionFit: At ease means free from anxiety or tension, comfortable.
